concept.name: Trade-through
concept.definition: An execution at a price inferior to a protected quotation displayed by another trading center - Regulation NMS Rule 600(b)(105) defines a trade-through as the purchase or sale of an NMS stock during regular trading hours at a price lower than a protected bid or higher than a protected offer. Rule 611 (the Order Protection Rule) requires trading centers to maintain policies reasonably designed to prevent trade-throughs.
concept.intuition: It is trading at a worse price while a better displayed price is available somewhere else in the national market system.
concept.mechanics: Trading centers prevent trade-throughs by routing to better-priced protected quotations (e.g. via intermarket sweep orders) before executing locally; Rule 611 lists exceptions, including executions during crossed markets, ISO routings, stopped orders, and quotes that flickered to an inferior price within one second prior.
concept.failure_modes: Consolidated-feed latency can make a quote appear tradeable when it is already gone (or vice versa), so mechanical trade-through protection can force routing to trivially small or stale protected quotes; the rule protects only top-of-book displayed prices, not depth.
concept.misconceptions: Rule 611 does not guarantee best execution for institutional size - it protects only the displayed protected quotation, and it applies to trading centers, which is distinct from a broker's broader best-execution duty.
concept.example: The NBO is $100.01 on NYSE; a trade executes at $100.03 on another venue without routing to NYSE first - a trade-through of the protected offer, absent an exception.
